checks_run.procedure: Confirm the assignment's operating-logic list through the integration and acceptance suites, my API probes and my in-process probe. The list covers: calculations, benefits, Finance validation, benefit types, SLAs, escalation, the blocker rule, meetings, corrective actions, status separation, BAU, after-closure behaviour, G5 and G6, waivers, the Modular G3 waiver, change requests, dashboards and traceability. checks_run.expected: The rules match their sources, and the observations and partial disclosures are acceptable.

The A01-A14 acceptance and backend suites pass 1985/1985. No API, worker, shared or DB module changed since round 5. The rules hold:
- RAG comes from the KPI trajectory, never from completion; a KPI with actuals but no trajectory stays Unknown (B0095, M0247).
- Forecast, submitted, upside and scenario values never count as validated.
- Finance validation is FIN-only, and an amendment keeps the chain.
- A non-financial benefit is n/a.
- Allocations over 100 % are refused, and links over 110 %.
- Escalation happens once, to the next authority, in working days on the calendar (B0099 SLAs).
- The blocker rule (N=2) creates exactly one T16 ask, also on a re-run (B0102 'Escalate decisions, not status').

QA-C O-2 (a transformation stays draft through G1-G6 until it is activated) is acceptable. The playbook defines phases and gates (B0010-B0016), not a record lifecycle. The DG1-approved explicit transition draft->active is the activation, and phase and gate progress are shown separately (the screenshots show 'Draft – not submitted' next to the phase).

QA-B (409 on approving a Draft gate) is the DG2-approved state-conflict contract. REQ-S04-010 only requires a rejection, so the code is not a source deviation.

The register's partial disclosures (PB-065, PB-066, PB-075, S04-010, S04-014, S07-005, S07-007, S07-015, S08-006, S08-015, S13-003, S15-008, S20-011) are byte-unchanged since round 5, honest and acceptable. checks_run.procedure: Trace the worker's start-up 'TimeoutNaNWarning' and measure its effect. Start a fresh disposable stack with the real worker under node --trace-warnings and wait 15 s. Sample pg_stat_database (db mth) transactions and the worker's /proc CPU ticks over 20 s with the worker running, then over 20 s with it SIGSTOPped as the baseline. Then a control run: the same, with only 'superviseIntervalSeconds: 60' added to the built worker's PgBoss options in the disposable clone, reverted afterwards (cmp identical). Read apps/worker/src/main.ts, queues/platform.ts and pg-boss 11.0.0's attorney.js and boss.js.
checks_run.command: WORKER=1 bash docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG4/domain/round-6/with-stack-trace.sh bash …/round-6/measure-supervise.sh; the same with the control patch (measure-supervise-control60.log); git grep -A12 'new PgBoss' 475f549^ -- apps/worker/src
checks_run.environment: Disposable stacks (PG 26401, API 26402, synthetic dev seed, the real worker, no probe activity); Node 24.21.0; pg-boss 11.0.0 as pinned in the lockfile; load average ~13-17.
checks_run.expected: The measurement and the control run exit 0 and show where the idle load comes from. Any defect is recorded as a finding.
checks_run.actual:
Both runs exit 0, so this probe PASSES. What it measured is a defect, raised as F-DG4-128 (Medium, not mandatory, REQ-S16-005, owner backend-workflow-engineer).

The trace: setInterval ← Boss.start (pg-boss src/boss.js:46) ← PgBoss.start ← apps/worker/dist/main.js. main.ts calls createBoss(config.databaseUrl!) with no options. createBoss sets supervise: true and passes superviseIntervalSeconds only when a caller gives it. pg-boss 11.0.0 defaults the maintenance, monitor and queueCache intervals, but not the supervise interval. The result is NaN, which Node turns into 1 ms, and supervision passes run back to back.

The measurements, each over 20 s:
- shipped worker, idle: 126,835 transactions (6,341/s) and 1,175 CPU ticks (about 0.59 core). The sampled statements are pg-boss's 'UPDATE pgboss.queue SET monitor_on/maintain_on = now() …' and its getQueues SELECT;
- worker SIGSTOPped: 1,090 (54/s) and 0 ticks;
- control (60 s interval): 333 (16/s) and 13 ticks, and the warning is gone.

The functional behaviour is correct, and the integration tests never use this default (they set superviseIntervalSeconds: 1). The configuration predates DG4 (475f549^), but REQ-S16-005's final gate is DG4. I judge it non-blocking for DG4, because nothing is lost, miscalculated or exposed, but it should be repaired: in production it is continuous database churn and CPU use. My round-4 and round-5 records dismissed this warning; that was an error, corrected here.

summary: PASS, with one new non-blocking finding. Candidate f966fe57 (1472 files) was verified in a complete clone, before and after the runs. The FE-R9B repair changes three session tests only and weakens nothing: Y1c keeps its 2-/me bound and adds stricter order checks, and a new case asserts D-077 item 3 directly. Validators PASS (register DG4; historical DG3, DG2, DG1). Node 24: unit 2917/2917, plus formula 259 with 2 by-design skips. Node 22: 5 load failures (architecture 30 s timeout; four web findBy timeouts) at load ~30, each passing alone twice, disclosed. Integration 1985/1985, my in-process probe included. Real-stack probes, the same ids as round 5: dom-api 49/49, dom-ui 38/38 (57 EN + 57 AR screenshots), dom-gross4 131/131, dom-pct 4/4, dom-kpiunit 51/51, dom-r5b 57/57. The T10 areas and forum layers are seeded word for word from B0095 and B0093. New: F-DG4-128 (Medium, not mandatory, REQ-S16-005). The shipped worker leaves pg-boss's superviseIntervalSeconds unset, so supervision runs every 1 ms: about 6,300 database transactions/s and 0.6 core while idle, against 16/s with a 60 s interval. It predates DG4, and my earlier rounds dismissed its warning wrongly.
